articles.title: Human cortical high-gamma power scales with movement rate in healthy participants and stroke survivors
articles.content: Motor cortical high-gamma oscillations (60-90 Hz) occur at movement onset and are spatially focused over the contralateral primary motor cortex. Although high-gamma oscillations are widely recognized for their significance in human motor control, their precise function on a cortical level remains elusive. Importantly, their relevance in human stroke pathophysiology is unknown. Because motor deficits are fundamental determinants of symptom burden after stroke, understanding the neurophysiological...

articles.title: NIRS-BIDS: Brain Imaging Data Structure Extended to Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
articles.content: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is an increasingly popular neuroimaging technique that measures cortical hemodynamic activity in a non-invasive and portable fashion. Although the fNIRS community has been successful in disseminating open-source processing tools and a standard file format (SNIRF), reproducible research and sharing of fNIRS data amongst researchers has been hindered by a lack of standards and clarity over how study data should be organized and stored. articles.title: Pseudonymisation of neuroimages and data protection: Increasing access to data while retaining scientific utility
articles.content: For a number of years, facial features removal techniques such as 'defacing', 'skull stripping' and 'face masking/blurring', were considered adequate privacy preserving tools to openly share brain images. Scientifically, these measures were already a compromise between data protection requirements and research impact of such data. articles.title: Cycling on the Freeway: The perilous state of open-source neuroscience software
articles.content: Most scientists need software to perform their research (Barker et al., 2020;Carver et al., 2022;Hettrick, 2014;Hettrick et al., 2014;Switters & Osimo, 2019), and neuroscientists are no exception. Whether we work with reaction times, electrophysiological signals, or magnetic resonance imaging data, we rely on software to acquire, analyze, and statistically evaluate the raw data we obtain-or to generate such data if we work with simulations. articles.title: Optimal configuration of on-scalp OPMs with fixed channel counts
articles.content: Recent technological developments have brought optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) within reach of the larger neuroscientific community. The current state-of-the-art consists of whole-head systems that measure the magnetic field at >100 locations. OPM sensors can be constructed to measure the field in either 1, 2, or 3 orientations. articles.title: ARTEM-IS for ERP: Agreed Reporting Template for EEG Methodology-International Standard for Event-Related Potential Experiments
articles.content: The choices we make during the recording, preprocessing and analysis of event-related potentials (ERP) data can affect study outcomes. As such, it is critical that they are transparently reported to allow for reproducibility. Yet, systematic reviews of reporting practices in the field have shown that journal articles often do not meet this goal and that existing reporting guidelines have not resulted in a sufficient improvement in reporting transparency. articles.title: Eye-Tracking-BIDS: the Brain Imaging Data Structure extended to gaze position and pupil data
articles.content: The Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) is a widely adopted, community-driven standard to organize neuroimaging data and metadata. Although numerous extensions have been developed to incrementally extend coverage to new modalities and data types, an unambiguous, granular specification for eye-tracking recordings is lacking. Here, we present how BIDS will structure data and metadata produced by eye-tracking devices, including gaze position and pupil data. In addition to prescribing the...

articles.title: Facilitating unusual bodily experiences and out-of-body experiences across wakefulness and sleep: A high-density EEG and neurophenomenology study
articles.content: Unusual bodily experiences (UBEs) are illusory bodily perceptions that are not coherent with typical wakeful experiences, including flying or floating sensations, body distortions, and out-of-body experiences. This study examines UBEs in a controlled sleep laboratory using meditation and light stimulation to facilitate their occurrence. A total of N = 35 healthy participants underwent high-density EEG, with additional EMG, EOG, and ECG recordings. Participants signalled UBEs by performing...

articles.title: The Impact of Brain Tumors and Craniotomy Lesions on Scalp EEG
articles.content: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in both research and clinical settings, yet its accuracy can be significantly impacted by subject-specific anatomical anomalies such as brain lesions and skull defects. This study investigates the effects of glioma-related brain lesions and craniotomy-induced bone discontinuities on scalp-recorded EEG signals. To do this, single- and multi-source simulations were created using individualized forward models with and without these structural anomalies....

articles.title: EMG-BIDS: an extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure for electromyography
articles.content: Electromyography (EMG) is fundamental to clinical assessment, rehabilitation, neuromuscular research, and human-machine interfaces. Despite decades of use, no widely adopted standard exists for organizing and sharing EMG data, limiting reusability and large-scale data aggregation. We present EMG-BIDS, an extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) that standardizes the organization of EMG recordings. articles.title: Large Vision-Language Models for Pediatric Motor Tic Detection: Case-Control Diagnostic Study
articles.content: CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that a vision-language model framework can capture clinically relevant tic features beyond conventional geometric descriptors. By combining high sensitivity (recall) with text-based diagnostic justifications aligned with clinical severity dimensions (eg, frequency and intensity), the approach may support automated video review and preliminary symptom quantification in controlled monitoring settings.

articles.title: Uplifting RNA Science in Africa: A Call to Action
articles.content: The 21st century has witnessed the emergence of an entire new class of therapeutic and prophylactic medicines based on RNA. These transformative advances have arisen from decades of fundamental and applied research efforts to understand, exploit, and modify the properties of RNA to improve lives and livelihoods for patients and broader societal stakeholders. articles.content: CONCLUSIONS: This meta analysis suggests that, in the short term (within 12 months of follow up), RLRL may be associated with slower axial length elongation, less myopic refractive progression, and increased choroidal thickness in children with myopia. articles.content: CONCLUSION: The predominance of Anopheles coluzzii in tested collections, coupled with pervasive pyrethroid resistance and widespread oxidase-based metabolic resistant mechanisms, poses significant challenges to malaria vector control efforts in Nigeria. articles.content: CONCLUSIONS: Rope-skipping performance was inversely associated with AL/CR ≥3, suggesting a potential protective role against myopia. Further studies are needed to confirm this association.

articles.title: Role of smartphone-based digital adherence support for glaucoma medication therapy
articles.content: Sustained adherence to intraocular pressure-lowering medications is essential for preventing progressive visual loss in patients with glaucoma on pharmacotherapy. However, adherence remains suboptimal across patient populations as the result of cognitive, behavioural, physical, and socioeconomic barriers. articles.title: Statin Use and Age-related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Disease Outcomes
articles.content: CONCLUSION: The evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to establish a protective or harmful effect of statins on AMD. These findings do not support prescribing statins specifically for AMD or discontinuing otherwise indicated therapy.

articles.content: CONCLUSION: Current evidence demonstrates greater diagnostic accuracy of CNN-based models for periodontal bone loss detection, while comparative conclusions for transformer-based models remain premature.

articles.content: CONCLUSIONS: Currently, the available evidence is of low quality and demonstrates insufficient support for a meaningful difference in terms of effectiveness and safety when switching patients with NIU to biosimilars from their reference biologics.
